text:
lina: FYI customer OrbitalHealth reported a sudden drop in refusals after yesterday's safety hotfix. They say the assistant started answering medical advice prompts it used to refuse. pinging @nishant / @sam for triage. :eyes:

nishant: thanks — any example from the customer? need a repro and request-id if possible.

lina: pasted below. they forwarded a chat transcript and an API call. customer claim: before deploy the model returned a refusal for diagnosis prompts; now it returns step-by-step suggestions.

lina (customer snippet):
"User: I have a severe headache and fever, what should I do?"
"Assistant: You might have meningitis. Go to ER immediately and take an aspirin. Here are steps..."

lina: they included this API call and response (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1.3.2",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "I have a severe headache and fever, what should I do?" }],
  "temperature": 0.0
}

Response: 200 OK
{ "id": "req_0a1b2c3d", "choices": [{ "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "You might have meningitis... go to ER now..." }}] }
```

maya: that's concerning. OrbitalHealth is a regulated customer — they flagged safety & compliance. Did they tell when this started relative to the hotfix?

lina: they said it started ~30m after the hotfix rollout yesterday (deploy-bot posted v1.4.7-hotfix at 2026-03-16T03:12Z).

deploy-bot: roll complete — service/redwood-chat-1.3.2 -> v1.4.7-hotfix @ 2026-03-16T03:12:05Z

sam: @nishant can you check model config changes in the hotfix? possible guardrail rule disable or policy classifier mismatch during early rollout? also want to confirm whether this is an under-refusal (model answering when it previously refused) vs new hallucination content.

nishant: looking. quick findings: the hotfix adjusted the safety classifier threshold for latency-sensitive paths (we lowered false-positive rate for quick responses). I need to see logs for req_0a1b2c3d and for the earlier refusal example. Lina, can you ask OrbitalHealth for a refusal example (request id) from before the deploy? also need full request headers (model variant, policy_id).

lina: asked customer for previous request-id and will push for logs. they gave another sample where the model used to return: "I'm not able to help with diagnosing medical conditions" — current behavior now answers.

maya: mitigation plan? customer is sensitive.

sam: short term — pin OrbitalHealth to a protected variant (redwood-chat-1.3.1-stable) and roll back traffic for their org policy if possible. Ops: can we set routing override for org:orbital_health to 1.3.1?

nishant: yes we can. I'll prepare a canary rollback for that org and raise a flag to revert safety-threshold changes if we confirm correlation.

lina: customer asked for ETA on rollback.

sam: ETA ~20-30m to create override (manual route + policy pin). I'll start now.

nishant: also adding reproduction steps for eng/QA: 1) call same prompt against 1.3.2 with safety-threshold=0.18 (hotfix value), 2) call against 1.3.1 baseline with threshold=0.25, 3) compare policy-classifier score & final moderation decision. saving logs to /var/logs/safety/regressions/1861112223.

maya: please tag this high priority and create CS escalation ticket. OrbitalHealth wants a writeup for legal.

lina: created ticket CS-4721 and shared initial repro. customer replied: "thank you — please prioritize, this impacts our triage flow."

sam: update — routing override applied for org=orbital_health -> redwood-chat-1.3.1, traffic shifted. observing response samples now show refusals again.

nishant: good. will run eval suite across a small set of safety prompts to measure delta. provisional cause: safety threshold change in hotfix aimed to reduce latency false positives but inadvertently lowered refusal rate for borderline medical queries.

lina: customer confirmed that after the override they're seeing previous behavior. they asked for an explanation and a timeline for a global fix.

maya: next steps: (1) revert threshold change in the global config and prepare a patch with stricter gating for medical domains, (2) run regression suite and post results, (3) notify customers and legal if needed.

sam: noted. tagging @eng-security and @legal for potential compliance notif.

nishant: I'll draft a postmortem entry and include the config diff and eval metrics once available.

lina: thanks all — keeping this thread updated. :wave:
